messages.subject: A spatio besag model
parts:
Hello
I'm a bit confusing :)
i want to estimate a model with a binary dependent variable. The observations are taken for 9 years and every year i have 150 observation
so
y_ij is the observed variable 
j=1,..., 9
i= 1,..., n_j
with n_j=150 for every j 
For every year i want to obtain a prevision for a grid of 10000, the same grid for all the years. I suppose there is a spatial dependance and, for now, there is not temporal dependence.
I would use a besag model but i am not sure how i should do.

My idea is this:
formula <-  y ~ f(ind, model="besag", graph=graph, param=c(0.1,0.1))
where y is a vector contains the observed points and NAs for the unobserved. 
I suppose the same precision and the same graph  for every year. 
I don't understand how use the besag model.  Is the graph for the 10000 observations or the 90000 observations? and what are in this case the values in ind? maybe and indicator such as c(1:10000, times=9).

Thanks

> i want to estimate a model with a binary dependent variable. The
> observations are taken for 9 years and every year i have 150
> observation
> so
> y_ij is the observed variable
> j=1,..., 9
> i= 1,..., n_j
> with n_j=150 for every j
> For every year i want to obtain a prevision for a grid of 10000, the
> same grid for all the years. I suppose there is a spatial dependance
> and, for now, there is not temporal dependence.
> I would use a besag model but i am not sure how i should do.
>
>
> My idea is this:
> formula <- y ~ f(ind, model="besag", graph=graph, param=c(0.1,0.1))
> where y is a vector contains the observed points and NAs for the
> unobserved.
> I suppose the same precision and the same graph for every year.
>
> I don't understand how use the besag model. Is the graph for the
> 10000 observations or the 90000 observations? and what are in this
> case the values in ind? maybe and indicator such as c(1:10000,
> times=9).

I think the formula is what you want. the besag model for a lattice is
not implemented but for a general graph it is.

Here is how to generate a graph-file for a regular lattice with Rows and
Columns:

> R = toeplitz(c(1,1,0,0,0,0,0))
> C = toeplitz(c(1,1,0,0))
> Q = kronecker(R,C)
> inla.spy(Q)
> graph = inla.read.graph(Q)
> inla.write.graph(graph, filename="graph.txt", mode="ascii")


H
